name: Beef burgers with sweet potato wedges
summary: Lean beef patties in wholewheat rolls with lettuce, tomato and onion, served with paprika-roasted sweet potato wedges and a crunchy cabbage and carrot slaw.
about: The hamburger, a seasoned beef patty in a soft bun, is American in origin. Made at home, the patty is simply seasoned lean mince, and sweet potato wedges roasted in a little olive oil take the place of deep-fried chips.

ingredients.name: Sweet potatoes
ingredients.note: scrubbed and cut into wedges, skin on

steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C if your oven is a fan oven). Toss the sweet potato wedges with the olive oil, paprika and salt on a large baking tray and spread them out in a single layer.
Roast for 30–35 minutes, turning them halfway, until golden at the edges and soft when pierced with a knife.
While they roast, make the slaw: put the cabbage and carrots in a bowl, whisk the olive oil, vinegar, mustard and a pinch of salt together, pour it over and toss well.

Put the mince, grated onion, garlic, salt and pepper in a bowl and mix lightly with your hands until just combined; overworking makes the burgers tough. Shape into 4 patties about 2 cm thick and a little wider than the rolls, press a shallow dent into the middle of each and chill for 10 minutes.

When the wedges have about 15 minutes left, heat a griddle pan or large frying pan over medium-high heat for 2 minutes. Brush the patties with the oil and cook for 4–5 minutes a side without pressing them, until well browned and cooked right through with no pink in the middle.
Lift the burgers onto a plate, then toast the cut sides of the rolls in the same pan for about 1 minute, until lightly golden.
Fill each roll with lettuce, a burger, tomato and red onion, and serve with the wedges and slaw.
prepNote: Shape the patties up to a day ahead, or freeze them between sheets of baking paper for up to 3 months.
